script.title: Chapter 23: First Campaign for the Tiger

panels.description: Wide, full page width. The Kayamkulam frontier in dry morning light: rolling ridges of red earth, gold grass, thin threads of smoke from small village fires. On the nearest ridge, the raw new laterite wall of a Travancore fort rising behind bamboo scaffolding, masons small on it. Below, a local chief's tiled house among pepper gardens, its people standing in the yard looking up at the wall.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The Kayamkulam frontier smelled different from the coast. Less salt, more dust.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The houses here owed the king less by habit than by calculation.

panels.description: The fort courtyard. An older Marakkar trader (a coastal Muslim: grey beard, bare-headed, bare-chested, checked lungi, a towel over one shoulder, no coat, no scar) warms his hands around a clay cup of spiced buttermilk and talks up at Nagoji. Nagoji is now Ananthan Pillai: Kerala topknot, first grey at the temples, NO turban, NO red sash, white mundu hitched for riding, cream shoulder cloth, silver chain of office, talwar at his hip. Clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, small gold ear stud. The chapter 22 wounds have healed: no bandage, only a thin pale line across his LEFT palm.

copy.speaker: TRADER
copy.text: Kollamkara Raja is entertaining foreign visitors. Men with pale faces and boxes of cloth.

copy.speaker: TRADER
copy.text: They come up the river at night.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Dutch?

panels.description: The trader, close, shrugging over his cup.

copy.speaker: TRADER
copy.text: Their ships sit off the coast these days with papers instead of cannons. But their smaller craft still wander.

copy.speaker: TRADER
copy.text: Company men do not forget how to look for gaps.

panels.description: A shaded verandah off the courtyard. Ramayyan Dalawa (thin, sharp fine features, receding hair, plain white cloth) in the foreground, fingers tapping on a palm-leaf bundle. Behind him Marthanda Varma (V13 face, cream and gold, gold necklaces, bare-headed, his hair in a side knot above his left ear, no turban, no crest) turns his head to look straight out of the panel at Nagoji.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Kollamkara sits near Padmini's northern edge.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: If he tilts too far toward Dutch coin, they will have a foothold behind our forts.

panels.description: Varma, close, the faintest edge of amusement.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: You wanted a frontier. Here it is.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Go and see whether this raja needs reminding who sharpens his sword.

panels.description: Wide. The column on a red dirt track. Light, quick Maravar horse; Madurai lancers with tall spears and plain cloth pennons; a core of turbaned Maratha riders around Nagoji, who rides bare-headed among them on Kayal, his bay mare with the ochre red-brown coat. Nagoji (Ananthan Pillai look: Kerala topknot, first grey at the temples, NO turban, NO red sash, white mundu, cream shoulder cloth, silver chain of office, small gold ear stud, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache). Behind, on foot, Nair musketeers in white with long Indian matchlocks shouldered, and a light gun on a two-wheeled carriage drawn by bullocks. Padmini Amma rides beside Nagoji (her fifties, grey threading the thick hair coiled at her nape, simple gold, cotton sari hitched for riding, her long walking stick laid across the saddle).

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: My own Maratha riders had chosen this southern service with me. Their jokes still carried the hills.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: My lands lie between you and his. I would rather be there when your men look for grazing.

panels.description: Large, half the page. Dusk in a village between Padmini's lands and Kollamkara's hill. A modest temple festival. The shrine has a Kerala-style gatehouse with a low, sloping tiled roof and carved wooden figures on its gables, not a tall stone tower. Bright cloths tied between trees, oil lamps flickering in niches along the outer wall, drummers and nadaswaram players. Men and women circle the shrine with small clay lamps cupped in their hands, faces lit from below like the carved figures on the gables. A procession winds out of the sanctum: girls carrying a palanquin with a simple wooden image of the goddess decked in fresh flowers, older women behind with brass plates of rice and turmeric. Padmini, dismounted, has slipped into their line as if she had always been there. Men bow their heads as she passes.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It was not a grand thing like those I had heard of at Padmanabhapuram, but the scale did not blunt its power.

panels.description: Nagoji (topknot, no turban, no sash, white mundu, silver chain) and Ponnan (broad-shouldered Maravar, curly hair, NO topknot, thick moustache, clean chin, red shoulder cloth, white mundu hitched, short jacket, spear) reined in at the edge of the crowd. Behind them a tusker with a gold nettipattam on its forehead sways while children offer it bananas. The crowd shifts to make room, eyes flicking to the swords, then back to the goddess.

copy.speaker: PONNAN
copy.text: War does not stop for this.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: This does not stop for war either.

panels.description: A food stall. A small village boy running past has bumped into Yusuf Marakkar (a sea captain: tall and lean, white skullcap, neatly trimmed dark beard, short coat over a white tunic, no vest, no scar), one hand on a basket of sweet fried discs. He steadies the child with an easy smile, and over the boy's head catches the eye of someone out of frame and tips his head.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Yusuf Marakkar. Business never slept, not even when gods walked.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Had he come to pay respect, to listen, or to see which chiefs showed their faces? Perhaps all three.

panels.description: Padmini back at her horse, lamp glow behind her, eyes brighter than we have seen them.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Now we go remind men outside these walls that she is not the only one watching.

panels.description: Morning, a roadside. An overturned grain cart, spilled paddy, three shapes under cloths along the verge. Ponnan (curly hair, NO topknot, red shoulder cloth, short jacket, spear) crouches by one and lifts a strip of blue-and-white checked Dutch company cloth and a few silver coins from the dead man's waist knot. Nagoji (Ananthan Pillai look: Kerala topknot, first grey at the temples, NO turban, NO red sash, white mundu, cream shoulder cloth, silver chain of office, small gold ear stud, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache) mounted above him on Kayal, his bay mare with the ochre red-brown coat.

copy.speaker: PONNAN
copy.text: He wants us to know. He is not hiding this.

copy.speaker: PONNAN
copy.text: He wants the Maharaja to see Dutch colour in his quarrel.

panels.description: Nagoji (topknot, clean chin, thick moustache), looking north toward the hills.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: If we strike him, he can tell other chiefs that we did it at the Dutch's bidding.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: And if we do not, he can tell the Dutch we fear their anger.

panels.description: Wide, full width. A narrow valley where the road dips between two wooded slopes. A line of spearmen and archers across the path. On both slopes, men with long Indian matchlocks, smouldering slow-match coiled at their wrists. Banners of bright plain cloth on tall poles in a hot wind. In the exact centre of the road, very small at this distance, a heavy man sits on a low stool.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Not a full ambush. That would have required more patience than they possessed.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It was an assertion, not an attempt to kill us all.

panels.description: Over the shoulder, from behind Nagoji in the saddle: his topknot, cream shoulder cloth and inclined head fill the near foreground, centre, with Kayal's ochre-bay neck below. At the left frame edge, Ponnan's spear and red shoulder cloth. At the right frame edge, a Nair captain (older and heavier than Nagoji, grey hair and grey moustache, bare-chested, round shield on his arm, no chain). Beyond them, close and centred, facing us: the Kollamkara Raja on his low stool. Heavy, flesh hanging a little over his waist sash, sharp eyes, bare-chested, white mundu with a broad gold-edged waist sash (no leather belt), heavy gold ear hoops and neck chains, a worn-hilted sword at the sash. He does not rise.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Raja.

copy.speaker: KOLLAMKARA
copy.text: Pillai. We heard the Maharaja had given a Maratha his Kayamkulam frontier.

copy.speaker: KOLLAMKARA
copy.text: Nice of him to send you to announce yourself.

panels.description: The raja (bare-chested, gold ear hoops, gold-edged waist sash) spreads his hands, comfortable on his stool. Behind him his spearmen grin.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: You block the king's road. That is one way to greet his officer.

copy.speaker: KOLLAMKARA
copy.text: I block no one's road. I sit on mine.

copy.speaker: KOLLAMKARA
copy.text: If the king wishes to pass, his horse can step around me.

panels.description: The raja, close (gold ear hoops, neck chains), eyes narrowing a fraction.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: And if Dutch coin passes along this road at night? Does that belong to you as well?

copy.speaker: KOLLAMKARA
copy.text: Dutch coin spends in our markets. As does Marakkar coin. As does Brahmin coin.

panels.description: Low angle from the slope: a Kollamkara musketman's long Indian matchlock in the near foreground, its slow-match smouldering. Below and beyond the barrel, Ponnan (curly hair, NO topknot, red shoulder cloth, short jacket) shifting his weight in the saddle, spear hand tightening. Beside him Nagoji (Ananthan Pillai look: Kerala topknot, first grey at the temples, NO turban, NO red sash, white mundu, cream shoulder cloth, silver chain of office, small gold ear stud, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache) on Kayal, his bay mare with the ochre red-brown coat, lifts one hand slightly without looking at him.

copy.speaker: KOLLAMKARA (off)
copy.text: The grain you send north does not ask whose hand dropped the money it buys. Why should I?

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: The king does not object to trade. He objects to men using foreign guns to settle local quarrels.

panels.description: Reverse wide, from behind the raja's stool: his broad bare back and gold-edged sash in the near foreground. Facing us down the road, Nagoji (topknot, no turban, no sash, white mundu, silver chain) on Kayal gestures back the way they came. Behind him the Travancore column, the Nair musketeers and the small gun on its bullock carriage. Matchlock barrels on both slopes frame the shot.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Travancore men lie dead on that road you raided. Their powder has company smell on it.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: That is not trade. That is provocation.

panels.description: The raja, close. For an instant his eyes drop, toward the road where the convoy died. The flicker only: his jaw has not yet set.

copy.speaker: KOLLAMKARA
copy.text: They took more than their due. The new walls demand more from us than the old ones did.

copy.speaker: KOLLAMKARA
copy.text: If the king wants to tighten his hand, he should expect us to wriggle.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. The raja leaning forward on the stool, jaw clenched, pride back in his face. INSET, lower corner, small, with a hard border and desaturated to sepia so it reads as memory, separate from the valley: Colachel beach in powder smoke, Kollamkara spearmen and Travancore Nairs in one line.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: If you wriggle into Dutch arms, do not be surprised when their grip leaves marks.

copy.speaker: KOLLAMKARA
copy.text: You come here with horse and muskets and speak as if we are children.

copy.speaker: KOLLAMKARA
copy.text: You forget that my men bled at Colachel too.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (on the inset)
copy.text: He was not wrong.

panels.description: Low angle up the slope: Kollamkara musketmen with long Indian matchlocks, slow-match smouldering at their wrists, shifting their weight, fingers near the firing levers. In the foreground the back of Nagoji's head, turned up toward them (Ananthan Pillai look: Kerala topknot, first grey at the temples, NO turban, NO red sash, white mundu, cream shoulder cloth, silver chain of office, small gold ear stud, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache).

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: We do not forget. Which is why the king sent me to talk before cannons.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: We are giving you the courtesy of argument first. Do not mistake it for fear.

panels.description: The raja's point of view, past Nagoji's shoulder (topknot, cream shoulder cloth): the Travancore musketeers, the small gun, and under a nearby tree Padmini on her horse, face unreadable. INSET, lower corner, warmer and softer: years earlier, a younger Padmini with black hair on a canal bank, stick pointed at a thinner, younger Kollamkara.

copy.speaker: PADMINI (inset, past)
copy.text: If you fight them, you fight me.

copy.speaker: PADMINI (inset, past)
copy.text: When you come to their aid, you spill your blood on my soil. Do not forget whose ground you stand on.

panels.description: The raja, shoulders tight now, glancing at the strip of land where the two domains brush.

copy.speaker: KOLLAMKARA
copy.text: What do you want, Pillai?

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: Your men off the road. Your promise that you will not use Dutch muskets on Travancore caravans.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: And if company men come again, they come as merchants, not as your private army.

panels.description: Two-shot, the stool and the horse: the raja looking up at Nagoji (topknot, no turban, no sash, white mundu, silver chain) on Kayal, his ochre-bay mare.

copy.speaker: KOLLAMKARA
copy.text: And what does the king give?

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: The same thing he gave at Colachel.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Nagoji, close, level (topknot, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, gold ear stud).

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Proof that when Dutch turn from coins to guns, they find more sand in their mouths than pepper.

panels.description: The raja snorts and pushes himself up from his stool. Nagoji (Ananthan Pillai look: Kerala topknot, first grey at the temples, NO turban, NO red sash, white mundu, cream shoulder cloth, silver chain of office, small gold ear stud, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache) watching him from the saddle.

copy.speaker: KOLLAMKARA
copy.text: You speak well for a man from the hills. Too well. It makes me suspect you have Ramayyan's ink on your tongue.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I have my own words. He just helps me keep track of where they land.

panels.description: Wide. The raja waving a hand. His line of spearmen parting slowly down the middle of the road.

copy.speaker: KOLLAMKARA
copy.text: Stand aside. Let the king's horse pass.

copy.speaker: KOLLAMKARA
copy.text: Only fools stand in front of a cannon to prove a point.

panels.description: Riding through the gap, spear points close on both sides. Ponnan (curly hair, NO topknot, red shoulder cloth, short jacket, spear) leaning toward Nagoji (topknot, no turban, no sash, white mundu, silver chain) on Kayal.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It felt less like victory than like being allowed to step over a tripwire that could be reset behind us.

copy.speaker: PONNAN
copy.text: That was not the last of him.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: No. But it is not today.

panels.description: Wide, full width. From a ridge: thick black columns of smoke above a strip of pepper gardens along a canal. Far below, raiders in plain cloth withdrawing into the scrub, small and unhurried.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: We did not have to wait long for today.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Two weeks later.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Kollamkara's men. No company colours, no Dutch muskets. But the message was clear enough: you do not frighten me with your cannon.

panels.description: The burned gardens up close: vines torched, support poles cut, red soil trampled. Two of Padmini's men lie still near the path, a farmer drawing a cloth over one (no wounds shown). Padmini in the foreground, her long walking stick gripped white-knuckled, voice shaking with restrained fury.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: He could not strike at the king. So he struck at me instead.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: He thinks you will hesitate to chase him into his own scrub.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: He was wrong.

panels.description: Wide. Galloping along a narrow track between red rock outcrops, branches whipping at the riders' faces, hooves throwing spray from a shallow stream over mossy stones.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The chase that followed was not like Colachel.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: No neat lines. No open beach. No clear horizon.

panels.description: A bend in the track. Half a dozen men burst from cover firing long matchlocks at close range, white powder smoke, arrows flying from a side thicket. Two Travancore horsemen are hit: one thrown backwards out of the saddle, hands at his chest; the other pitching sideways, a foot caught in his stirrup as his horse bolts.

Nagoji (Ananthan Pillai look: Kerala topknot, first grey at the temples, NO turban, NO red sash, white mundu, cream shoulder cloth, silver chain of office, small gold ear stud, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache) driving Kayal, his bay mare with the ochre red-brown coat, straight at the nearest shooter, talwar out, the horse filling the frame toward us. The shooter has dropped his empty matchlock and is grabbing for his sword, eyes wide.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Too slow.

panels.description: Ponnan's rescue is the focal action, in the foreground: Ponnan (curly hair, NO topknot, red shoulder cloth, short jacket), leaning from his saddle, has cut the stirrup strap with his blade and is hauling the dragged rider clear. At the frame edge, only spear points and dust where his Maravar riders sweep the flank. Far back in the road, small, the shooter lies still, face down.

Regrouping on the far side of the bend. Ponnan (curly hair, red shoulder cloth, short jacket) rides up, sweat streaking his horse's neck, breathing hard. Nagoji (topknot, no turban, no sash, white mundu, silver chain) on Kayal.

copy.speaker: PONNAN
copy.text: Your Deccan tricks work in these hills too.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Without you on that flank, half my plans would be corpses in the road.

copy.speaker: PONNAN
copy.text: Good. Remember that when the king counts whose men bled here.

panels.description: Wide. Late afternoon. A ridge above a shallow valley choked with low thorn bushes and rocky outcrops. Riders reined in along the crest, horses blowing hard. Among them Nagoji (Ananthan Pillai look: Kerala topknot, first grey at the temples, NO turban, NO red sash, white mundu, cream shoulder cloth, silver chain of office, small gold ear stud, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache) on Kayal, and Ponnan (curly hair, NO topknot, red shoulder cloth, short jacket, spear).

copy.speaker: PONNAN
copy.text: If we go in there blind, we will bleed for every shrub.

panels.description: Padmini at the rear of the column, where she insisted on riding, eyes flinty.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: He chose this ground for that.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: He thinks you will either rush in and lose men or pull back and let him claim he held you.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off)
copy.text: We do neither.

panels.description: The light gun hauled into place on the ridge by its sweating crew. The gun captain sighting along the barrel, not at a wall but at the thickest stand of scrub where the raiders' trail vanishes. Nagoji (topknot, no turban, no sash, white mundu, silver chain) beside him.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: We do not need to kill them all. Just remind them that this terrain does not belong only to them.

panels.description: Wide. The gun fires: flame, a great bank of smoke, and across the valley a burst of birds exploding out of the trees.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The cannon could not kill a whole band hidden in such cover. It could tear holes in their confidence.

panels.description: Nagoji (topknot, no turban, no sash, white mundu, silver chain) dismounted, talwar drawn, leading the first small group on foot down off the ridge into the thorn.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Now.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: In scrub like this, men die faster when you can smell each other's breath.

panels.description: Inside the thorn. Close, dim, green-brown. Thorns catching at cloth. A matchlock ball shreds the leaves beside the ear of Nagoji (Ananthan Pillai look: Kerala topknot, first grey at the temples, NO turban, NO red sash, white mundu, cream shoulder cloth, silver chain of office, small gold ear stud, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache).
A spearman lunges from behind a bush. Nagoji twists, the point scraping past his hip, his elbow already driving up toward the man's jaw. Freeze the instant before contact.

Two figures in silhouette against a wall of powder smoke: a raider with his sword raised high, and Nagoji stepping inside the swing. A low side light rims the raider's face so the ash smeared across it reads while both bodies stay dark. In the background a third figure, dagger in fist, slipping on a loose stone.

Nagoji (topknot, no turban, no sash, white mundu, silver chain), chest-up, close. Soot, sweat, and something in the eyes we have not seen before. Behind him, in soft focus, the three raiders of 13.2 and 13.3 lie down and still in the thorn: the spearman, the ash-faced swordsman, the man with the dagger. No wounds drawn; the stillness is the point.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The world narrowed. Heat, screams, powder smoke, fresh blood, all of it sang to something dark in me.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I was not just fighting. I was hunting.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. A young raider, no more than sixteen, thin and beardless, hair in a small knot, a torn brown shoulder cloth, cornered against a rock face. His sword is gone. His hands are up. His eyes are wide with terror.

copy.speaker: BOY
copy.text: Mercy!

panels.description: Nagoji (Ananthan Pillai look: Kerala topknot, first grey at the temples, NO turban, NO red sash, white mundu, cream shoulder cloth, silver chain of office, small gold ear stud, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, all of it soot-streaked), close, laughing: teeth bared, the ugliest we have ever seen him.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: A wet, ugly sound.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Mercy is for men who stay on their own land.

panels.description: Low angle from behind the boy: the talwar raised high over Nagoji's head against a white sky, the boy shrinking beneath it.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Not just to kill him. To split him to the navel.

panels.description: Tight insert: Ponnan's hand clamps onto Nagoji's sword wrist from out of frame, just above the talwar hilt. Only the arm shows: a short jacket sleeve and the edge of a red shoulder cloth. Iron-hard. The blade stops.

copy.speaker: PONNAN (off)
copy.text: Ananthan!

panels.description: Nagoji (topknot, no turban, no sash, white mundu, silver chain) spinning, ready to strike whoever it is. Ponnan (curly hair, NO topknot, red shoulder cloth, short jacket), face streaked with soot but eyes clear and hard, gripping Nagoji's wrist and forcing the blade down.

copy.speaker: PONNAN
copy.text: Look at him. He is a boy. He is beaten.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: He is an enemy.

panels.description: Ponnan (curly hair, red shoulder cloth, short jacket), close, still gripping the wrist, his voice cutting through.

copy.speaker: PONNAN
copy.text: He is not the Portuguese. We are not at Colachel, fighting white devils. These are men of the soil.

copy.speaker: PONNAN
copy.text: Kill him if you must, but do not butcher him like a dog.

panels.description: Nagoji (Ananthan Pillai look: Kerala topknot, first grey at the temples, NO turban, NO red sash, white mundu, cream shoulder cloth, silver chain of office, small gold ear stud, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache), shoulders dropped, staring down at the talwar in his own hand. The blade is dulled dark from edge to hilt, never rendered red. Beyond it, in soft focus, the boy sobbing against the rock.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The red receded, leaving me cold and shaking.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Go. Run before I remember who I am.

panels.description: The boy breaking free to the LEFT, clear of the blade: a bearded older raider (head cloth, bare chest) has his fist knotted in the boy's shoulder cloth, and the boy twists loose of it. On the RIGHT, Nagoji steps in, his talwar arcing only at the raider, whose body is cut off by the right panel border. The boy is fully visible, untouched and running.
The boy running harder, feet slipping on rock, disappearing into the thorn. Nagoji in the foreground, back to us, the talwar down at his side.

Sunset. The ridge. Far below on the valley floor, long rows of bodies being dragged into lines, many of them, small and cloth-covered at this distance. Padmini waiting on her horse. Nagoji (topknot, no turban, no sash, silver chain) climbing up to her on foot, his white mundu no longer white: dark stains soaked into the cloth and up both forearms to the elbows, dried dark, never rendered red, more than soot. She looks at him for a long moment.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Too much of the blood on me to be mine.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: You were thorough.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Not fear, exactly. Recognition.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: They will not come back.

panels.description: Ponnan (curly hair, NO topknot, red shoulder cloth, short jacket) wiping his spear on a cloth, quiet. Padmini turning her horse away.

copy.speaker: PONNAN
copy.text: No. Ghosts rarely raid.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Good. War is not a place for half-measures.

panels.description: Wide. The fort's pillared audience hall: laterite walls, a carved teak ceiling, a grey stone floor, a tall doorway at the far end. It is not the black-floored palace room of 20.4. Brittle air. Ramayyan (thin, sharp fine features, receding hair, plain white cloth) seated at a low desk with a palm-leaf bundle, its strips fanned open and the cord loosened, an iron stylus in his hand. Varma (V13 face, cream and gold, gold necklaces; a closed-door council, not a court audience, so bare-headed, his hair in a side knot above his left ear, no turban, no crest) pacing behind him. Nagoji (Ananthan Pillai look: Kerala topknot, first grey at the temples, NO turban, NO red sash, white mundu, cream shoulder cloth, silver chain of office, small gold ear stud, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache) standing stiffly, clean now; Padmini beside him with her chin high.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Weeks later.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: This report. It makes for... vivid reading.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: We secured the border.

panels.description: Varma stops pacing and turns. Cold eyes.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: You secured a massacre.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: We sent you to deter a chieftain, Pillai. Not to paint the rocks with the entrails of his farmers.

panels.description: Padmini cutting in. Ramayyan snapping back, stylus pointed.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: They were armed. They were raiders.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: They were potential subjects. Or at least, men whose cousins pay us tax.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: The market says the King's new Maratha captain is a butcher. That he enjoys the kill too much.

panels.description: Nagoji (topknot, no turban, no sash, white mundu, silver chain), the flush rising in his neck. INSET, lower corner, small, with a hard border and desaturated to sepia so it reads as memory, separate from the hall: the boy's raised hands against the rock face.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: It... got out of hand. The fighting was close. Confused. I lost myself.

copy.speaker: VARMA (off)
copy.text: You are a commander. You do not get the luxury of losing yourself. That is for foot soldiers and berserkers.

panels.description: Nagoji bowing his head. Ramayyan unmoved. Padmini's head already turning.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I apologise, Your Highness. It will not happen again.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: It better not.

copy.speaker: PADMINI (off)
copy.text: He has nothing to apologise for.

panels.description: All three men looking at her: Varma, Ramayyan, and Nagoji (Ananthan Pillai look: Kerala topknot, first grey at the temples, NO turban, NO red sash, white mundu, cream shoulder cloth, silver chain of office, small gold ear stud, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache). Padmini, eyes flashing.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: They burned my fields. They took foreign money to threaten our flank. Ananthan did what was necessary.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: If the price of safety is a few bloody rocks, I will pay it.

panels.description: Varma, quiet now, not unkind.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: We do not ask you to pay it, Amma. We ask you to remember that we are building a kingdom, not a graveyard.

panels.description: Padmini looking from the king to Nagoji, disgust on her face. At them for their softness, or at him for his apology; let the drawing leave it open.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Sometimes they are the same thing.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: I will not stand here and be scolded for surviving.

panels.description: Padmini's back, going out through the tall doorway of the audience hall, her long walking stick striking the grey stone floor. The three men left behind her, small in the hall: Varma, Ramayyan and Nagoji.
directions: No text. Hold the silence she leaves.

panels.description: Ramayyan waving a hand without looking up from the leaf. Nagoji (topknot, no turban, no sash, white mundu, silver chain) bowing low, palms joined at his chest, already turning to go.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Go, Ananthan. Clean yourself up.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: And pray that the next rumour speaks of your discipline, not your thirst.

panels.description: Night, a single lamp. Nagoji (Ananthan Pillai look: Kerala topknot, first grey at the temples, NO turban, NO red sash, white mundu, shoulder cloth set aside, silver chain of office, small gold ear stud, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache) at a basin, his knuckles scrubbed raw and red. The water is only faintly pink-tinged and already clearing at the rim.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I left that hall feeling smaller than I had in years.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: My knuckles stung, and still I could taste smoke at the back of my throat.

panels.description: Before dawn. Padmini in the doorway of his quarters, shawl pulled tight, eyes bright in the lamp glow. Her long walking stick is still and silent at her side. Nagoji (topknot, no turban, no sash, white mundu, silver chain) turning from the basin.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Do not let their scolding fool you.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: It was not scolding. It was judgment.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: In public. Yes.

panels.description: Padmini stepping in, voice low. Nagoji listening, the lamp between them.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: I went back to the king's rooms. Their doors do not hold words as well as stone holds arrows.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: The king asked if Kollamkara would raid that valley again. Ramayyan said no. Not after what the Maratha did to the last ones.

panels.description: Padmini leans close to Nagoji, as if the walls themselves were listening. Lamp between their faces.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: The king said a kingdom cannot be run by butchers.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Then he said it is very useful to have a man the enemy believes is one. "Let them fear the Tiger's claws."

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Over Nagoji's shoulder: his own two hands in the foreground, open, scrubbed, knuckles raw. The nails ridged from old torture, the Portuguese brand on the LEFT wrist, a faint pale line across the LEFT palm. Padmini beyond them, straightening, the shawl slipping from one shoulder.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: They will shame you when eyes are watching, and they will praise you when they want you sharp.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Do not let their need become your hunger.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Clean now, and still not clean.

panels.description: Wide, full width. The great Padmanabhaswamy temple under a hard sky: the gopuram, the ring of belikal offering stones, a line of temple elephants darker than night and draped in silks swaying in the gopuram's shade. A crowd pressing to see the royal party. Marthanda Varma (V13 varma-v1 face; temple dress: bare-chested, white mundu, white silk angavastram over one shoulder, heavy rings on his hands, sandal paste on the brow; NO peacock crest, NO spear) and beside him the heir (a boy of about ten, his uncle's sharp cheekbones, wide watchful eyes, small white silk mundu, a thin gold chain). At the outer perimeter with the escort's white-clad spearmen, Nagoji (Ananthan Pillai look: Kerala topknot, first grey at the temples, NO turban, NO red sash, white mundu, cream shoulder cloth, silver chain of office, small gold ear stud, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache).

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Peace is a fragile skin on a rotting fruit.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Three days later. I commanded the King's escort.

panels.description: The front of the crowd. One devotee (lean, bare-chested, white mundu, hair cropped close, NO moustache, three pale lines of ash across his brow) is moving: not running, flowing, like water finding a crack.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It happened in the space between two heartbeats.

panels.description: The same man (hair cropped close, no moustache, ash lines on his brow) clears the line of spears in one leap, a curved gutting knife coming out of his cloth.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: A chaver. A suicide warrior who has accepted death before he even draws his blade.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: His target was not the King.

panels.description: The heir (a boy of about ten, his uncle's sharp cheekbones, wide watchful eyes, small white silk mundu, a thin gold chain), frozen, eyes wide, the knife flashing down toward him.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It was the boy.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Varma (white silk angavastram, heavy rings) throwing his own body across the heir, turning his back and his LEFT shoulder to the falling blade. In the background, too far away, Nagoji (topknot, no turban, no sash, white mundu, silver chain) with his sword half clear of the scabbard.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Marthanda Varma did not shout. He did not call for guards.

panels.description: Varma spinning, ignoring the blade at the back of his LEFT shoulder (no wound drawn), driving his ringed fist into the chaver's face (hair cropped close, no moustache, ash lines on his brow). Spear points entering the panel from every edge.

Wide. A ring of spears lowered to the ground just out of frame; the body is never shown. Varma swaying, his RIGHT hand clamped to his LEFT shoulder over the white silk, a dark patch beneath his fingers kept in shadow. The heir (small white silk mundu, thin gold chain) clinging to his leg, sobbing. Ramayyan pushing through the crowd, ashen.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The silence that followed was more terrible than the scream.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Highness!

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: I am fine. Check the boy.

panels.description: Padmini, sharp with relief, pulling the heir (a boy of about ten, his uncle's sharp cheekbones, wide watchful eyes, small white silk mundu, a thin gold chain) into her arms.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: The Prince is unharmed.

panels.description: The palace room with the black polished floor and the ship-prow timber roof. Oil lamps. Varma (V13 face, bare-chested, bare-headed, his hair in a side knot above his left ear, no turban, no crest) on a low couch, physicians binding the back of his LEFT shoulder with pastes and cloth. Nagoji (Ananthan Pillai look: Kerala topknot, first grey at the temples, NO turban, NO red sash, white mundu, cream shoulder cloth, silver chain of office, small gold ear stud, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache) by a pillar. Ramayyan in the doorway, looking sick.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: An hour later.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The wound was deep but not mortal.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Well?

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: A chaver. From the north. A mark on his dagger hilt, and gold in his waist pouch that speaks of Kochi mints.

panels.description: Ramayyan, close, hesitating.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: But the style... the hatred...

copy.speaker: VARMA (off)
copy.text: Say it.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Thampi. One of the sons who fled. The brothers are dead, but their hate breeds in exile.

panels.description: Varma, eyes closed, face pale, the bandage on his LEFT shoulder pale in the lamplight. In the foreground an oil lamp flame sputtering.
Varma's eyes open. Whatever amusement was in them on page 1 is gone. Something older in its place.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: They struck at the child. They did not come for me, a man who can fight.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: They came for the future.

panels.description: Varma sitting up, pushing away the physician's restraining hand. Ramayyan and Nagoji (Ananthan Pillai look: Kerala topknot, first grey at the temples, NO turban, NO red sash, white mundu, cream shoulder cloth, silver chain of office, small gold ear stud, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache) leaning in.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Listen to me, Dalawa. And you, Pillai.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: I want a squad. Not soldiers. Chavers of our own. Or men who have forgotten how to sleep.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: To guard the Prince?

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: No. To hunt.

panels.description: High angle from the carved timber ceiling, looking straight down: lamp shadows sliding across the carved beams in the near foreground, and far below on the black floor, Varma small on the low couch, his LEFT shoulder bandaged, gazing up toward us. Ramayyan and Nagoji (topknot, no turban, no sash, white mundu, silver chain) leaning in on either side of him.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Go north. Find where these sons hide.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Find their wives. Find their children. Find anyone who carries a drop of Thampi blood.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Highness, the political fallout...

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Varma, close, his voice dropped to a whisper.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: There will be no politics. Because there will be no one left to complain.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: I want them gone, Ramayyan. Root and branch.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: If a babe in arms carries that name, I want it silenced.

panels.description: Nagoji (Ananthan Pillai look: Kerala topknot, first grey at the temples, NO turban, NO red sash, white mundu, cream shoulder cloth, silver chain of office, small gold ear stud, clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache), venturing, the scolding still fresh on his face.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: But... just days ago, you spoke against butchery.

panels.description: Chest-up on Varma on the couch: the bandage on his LEFT shoulder and the fingers of his RIGHT hand touching it both in frame, and his eyes still readable: hard, flat surfaces reflecting nothing.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: That was war, Pillai. War has rules. Men fight for land, for coin, for duty.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: This? This is not war. This is a weed trying to strangle my sapling. And for weeds, there is no treaty. There is only fire.

panels.description: Varma lying back, face pale but jaw set like the stone of his fort.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Kill them all. And when you are done, bring me the rings from their fingers so I know my nephew is safe.

panels.description: Nagoji (topknot, no turban, no sash, white mundu, silver chain) looking at Ramayyan. Ramayyan, grim, nodding slowly.
Full width, bottom. The corridor outside: the black floor gleaming under lamplight, Ramayyan and Nagoji (topknot, white mundu) walking out of the king's room, small in the long perspective.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: The Tiger has teeth.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: And claws.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: God help anyone who thinks they can clip them.
